reason: The repository wording says only that the Hardy-Littlewood circle method is a fundamental method of additive number theory. A method is not a proposition, and the intake intentionally leaves open the representation problem, domains, ordered binders, hypotheses, asymptotic or existence conclusion, local conditions, and error term. Selecting a Waring, Goldbach, partition, or abstract major/minor-arc theorem would substitute mathematics not present in the source.
unresolved_inputs: immutable primary-source edition and exact theorem/page or formula locator, with assumptions and errata reviewed
source-selected theorem family and exact representation or coefficient function
ordered binders, domains, number of summands, weights, and limiting regime
local-solubility and other hypotheses, including all boundary and degenerate cases
main term, singular series or integral normalization, uniformity, and exact error term
source-faithful Lean encoding and any alternate-encoding transports
lean_surface_assessment: Pinned mathlib exposes AddCircle, UnitAddCircle, AddCircle.haarAddCircle, fourier, fourierCoeff, and fourierCoeff_eq_intervalIntegral through Mathlib.Analysis.Fourier.AddCircle. IntakeProbe.lean re-elaborates these possible substrate APIs. They do not identify a source proposition, so the probe is not a canonical target and its import cannot be certified as the target's minimal import.
rejected_substitutions: an abstract schema that assumes major- and minor-arc estimates as fields or hypotheses
retry_condition: Pin and independently review one precise source theorem, freeze all of its conventions and boundary cases, then encode it with minimized pinned imports, serialize the elaborated expression, check source-faithful transports, and run hypothesis/domain/binder/boundary mutation tests.
